findings.summary: The stated pre-fix failure is factually wrong: a non-matching Select-String exits 0, and code page 437 decodes UTF-8 'café' as 'caf├⌐', not 'cafÃ©'.
findings.evidence: docs/briefs/B20261126-1034-b43-i162-pwsh-gates-utf8.loop-brief.md lines 27-29, 106-110 and 156-157 claim the mismatch exits 1 and show 'cafÃ©'. On the review machine, `chcp` prints `Active code page: 437`; `pwsh -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command '$x=[System.Text.Encoding]::GetEncoding(437).GetString([byte[]](0x63,0x61,0x66,0xC3,0xA9)); Write-Output $x'` prints `caf├⌐`; and `pwsh -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command "'caf' | Select-String -SimpleMatch 'café'"` prints nothing and exits 0.
findings.fix: Make the worked example state the actual pre-fix result (no match, exit 0 under this command), and correct the code-page-437 mojibake. State that the oracle wrapper, not Select-String's process exit, makes the base gate fail because the captured bytes are missing/wrong.

findings.section: Behaviour contract / U1 Gate; Shape task 1
findings.summary: The proposed gate does not prove all three required encodings and may pass before the fix on the stated Windows run environment, so plan acceptance can reject a correct planner rather than establish a planted failure.
findings.evidence: docs/briefs/B20261126-1034-b43-i162-pwsh-gates-utf8.loop-brief.md lines 89-95 require [Console]::OutputEncoding, [Console]::InputEncoding and $OutputEncoding to be BOM-less UTF-8, but lines 106-111 and 194-196 gate only the café native-output case, exit 3 and unchanged sh arguments. On the review machine, a fresh pwsh 7.7 process reports input 437, output 65001, $OutputEncoding 65001 and preamble length 0. Thus the café/output test can pass before the change while [Console]::InputEncoding remains 437. Current internal/state/gate.go lines 23-24 pass the recorded command unchanged and internal/state/gate_test.go lines 10-19 is the existing cross-platform argument test.
findings.fix: Add a deterministic U1 gate that asserts literal WebName/code-page and zero preamble for all three encodings inside each vloop-started PowerShell process, and add a PowerShell-to-native-stdin round trip for $OutputEncoding. Cover both `pwsh` and `powershell`; where an executable is unavailable, pin the generated -Command argument with the existing cross-platform test-double/argument mechanism. Name the wrapper assertion that fails on the base and pin the exact captured bytes, including the line ending or an explicit no-line-ending form.

decisions: vloop sets UTF-8 itself in the command it starts rather than requiring every gate author to do so; sound for the cross-repository defect, provided the setup is silent and failure-tolerant as contracted.
The behavior applies on every OS; sound because it gives both shell names one path and the brief still leaves other shells unchanged.
All three encodings use BOM-less UTF-8; sound, but the gate must explicitly prove each setting and both conversion directions.
The setup may live in the -Command prefix or another pwsh mechanism; sound as an implementation freedom, provided arbitrary recorded command semantics remain intact.
The café subject is the native-output fixture and git is addressed with -C in a temporary repository; sound as a fixture choice, but not sufficient by itself to prove the base failure.
